scope: Selected exact-allele functional observations, human phenotype observations and treatment examples. Experimental mechanism, clinical classification, phenotype attribution and treatment response are separate claims. This is not a comprehensive variant–phenotype database.

phenotypes.label: Reduced forced expiratory volume in one second
phenotypes.rationale: FEV1 is measured in the stated CF genotype cohort; the trial does not attribute every respiratory feature to this allele alone.

evidence.claim: G551D protein response supports potentiation of a channel gating defect; missense classification alone would not establish this mechanism.
Randomized participants with at least one G551D allele had a 10.6 percentage-point FEV1 advantage over placebo through week24. The other allele and disease background remain relevant.

cases.cells: Epithelial CFTR activity is implicated; this trial does not identify a single atlas epithelial subtype responsible for the endpoint.
limits: Functional response does not generalize to all CFTR variants.
FEV1 is a directly measured phenotype in the variant-selected trial cohort. The clinical outcome does not establish variant-specific cell-type causality or cellular rescue.

scope.assay: G551D gating response and genotype-selected randomized clinical trial

assessmentScenarios.label: Published STRIVE G551D cohort — ivacaftor 150 mg twice daily

gates.reason: G551D gating loss and the potentiator direction are established for this genotype-selected cohort.
Ivacaftor potentiates CFTR gating in the studied G551D context; this does not transfer to every CFTR allele.
STRIVE measured a pulmonary response to ivacaftor versus placebo in participants aged at least 12 years with at least one G551D allele.
Percent-predicted FEV1 improved by 10.6 percentage points versus placebo through week 24. This establishes cohort endpoint response, not individual eligibility or an atlas-cell mediator.

modifiers.reason: The randomized study measured the named pulmonary endpoint through week 24.
Direct genotype-selected randomized treatment evidence exists for this intervention and pulmonary endpoint.

phenotypes.label: Seizure

phenotypes.rationale: Seizures were measured in one affected patient; this is case evidence rather than proof that this allele alone determines the phenotype.

evidence.claim: Patient fibroblast RNA and functional assays supported correction of aberrant splicing and lysosomal dysfunction.
The uncontrolled individual-treatment report described reduced seizure frequency and duration.
A single case and fibroblast rescue do not establish reversal of neurodegeneration or rescue in an atlas-defined neuronal subtype.

cases.cells: Functional rescue was tested in patient-derived fibroblasts; direct human neuronal rescue was not demonstrated.
limits: No exact ClinVar variation match is asserted for the reported insertion.
Genomic coordinates and full insertion sequence are not normalized here.
The second allele and treatment timing matter; a truncating-variant label is not sufficient for splice-correction eligibility.

mechanismEvidence.notes: Reduced conventional sodium-channel function is the scoped finding, not a complete binary mechanism: R853Q also produced a noncanonical gating-pore current in another assay. Neuronal maturation and recording method change the observed excitability. Increasing expression therefore remains a direction hypothesis requiring intervention-specific testing.
mechanismEvidence.directionReason: Conventional current loss coexists with a noncanonical gating-pore current and assay-dependent neuronal excitability. This evidence does not resolve whether increasing or lowering SCN2A expression would restore the selected phenotype; the exact intervention requires testing.

scope.assay: RT-PCR, minigene, protein and NMD-inhibition assays

functionalObservations.intervention: NMD inhibition used as a diagnostic experiment
functionalObservations.claim: Exon 6 skipping produced a frameshift and transcript decay; RNA and MUNC18-1 protein were reduced by more than 40%.

evidence.claim: Primary functional evidence supports transcript loss; it does not demonstrate therapeutic splice correction.

cases.cells: Induced-neuron evidence does not identify an atlas subtype.
limits: The frozen ClinVar classification remains uncertain significance; this functional review does not overwrite it.
One patient observation cannot establish phenotype penetrance.
Blocking NMD does not prove that the resulting mutant transcript is safe or functional.

gates.reason: Exon 6 skipping and transcript decay were experimentally demonstrated. No splice-correcting treatment was tested.

modifiers.reason: Direct RNA and protein evidence identifies the splice defect, but preclinical evidence for a corrective ASO remains unknown: neither a corrective ASO nor phenotype rescue was tested. Defect characterization alone does not establish treatment maturity.

functionalObservations.assay: Brain RNA, seizure onset and survival
functionalObservations.intervention: Mouse-sequence Scn8a-lowering ASO by neonatal ICV injection
functionalObservations.timeFrame: Postnatal day 2; some mice redosed day 30
functionalObservations.claim: Transcript reduction delayed seizures and lethality in this model.

evidence.claim: Neonatal model benefit does not establish human delivery, safety or rescue of established disease.

cases.cells: Bulk brain RNA and global mutant activation do not isolate the sufficient neuronal subtype.
limits: The ASO sequence targets mouse Scn8a; this is not a verified human treatment.
Human variant identity and the homologous mouse construct are explicitly distinct.
Benefit in this model does not transfer to SCN8A loss-of-function alleles or every other gain-channel allele.
